sections.content: How many people are officers in armed forces?

29,565 people

Listed their occupation as "Officers in armed forces" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Officers in armed forces serve as commissioned officers in His Majesty�s armed forces, foreign and Commonwealth armed forces plan, direct, organise and administer military operations; and perform duties for which there is no civilian equivalent.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "officers in armed forces", there were more men than women, (86% compared with 14%).

This is different compared with the average for the wider occupation group of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 86% and women made up 14% of "officers in armed forces"
Across the whole working population, 52% are men and 48% are women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to officers in armed forces included:

  • Process operatives (other)
  • Sports players
  • Furniture makers and other craft woodworkers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women is most equally split:

  • Quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • Chartered and certified accountants
  • Conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally aged between 30 and 49 years

The occupation of "officers in armed forces" has more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as officers in armed forces, 18.2% were in this age group. The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "officers in armed forces" was 65 years and over.
